title: Which number does a stack of Mayan dots and a bar show?
description: A Mayan numeral of two dots, three dots and one bar is read from the bottom up, each set times its landmark. Keeko's doubt is that the numeral can be read from the top down.
teaching_notes: One idea: in the Mayan system the lowest set of symbols counts ones, the next counts twenties, and the next counts three hundred sixties. Watch for students who read the top set as the ones.

source: A Mayan numeral shows, from top to bottom, two dots, then three dots, then one bar. What number is it?
video_script.why: The child reads a Mayan numeral by giving each set of dots and bars its landmark, starting from the bottom, and adds the parts.
video_script.substitution: Read each set from the bottom up, multiply by its landmark one, twenty or three hundred sixty, and add.
video_script.anchor: the book's Mayan numeral: sets of dots and bars written one below the other
video_script.wrong_answer: one thousand eight hundred sixty two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads from the top, so the top set counts ones and the bottom set counts 360s: 2 x 1 + 3 x 20 + 5 x 360 = 1862, which is more than double the right value
video_script.payoff_line: Seven hundred twenty plus sixty plus five makes seven hundred eighty five.
maths_rules: a dot is 1 and a bar is 5; the sets are written one below the other
the lowest set counts 1s, the next counts 20s, the next counts 360s
bottom: one bar = 5; middle: three dots = 3; top: two dots = 2
Keeko's slip: reading from the top gives 2 x 1 + 3 x 20 + 5 x 360 = 2 + 60 + 1800 = 1862
video_script.design: One idea: the lowest set counts ones and each set above counts a bigger landmark. The stack stays on the board with its landmark labelled beside each set.

marks.stack: sets of symbols stack one above another

narration: <bookmark mark='symbols'/>The Mayans used a dot for one and a bar for five. With them they made the numbers from one to nineteen.
<bookmark mark='stack'/>Each set of symbols was written above the one before.
<bookmark mark='land'/>The lowest set counts ones, the next set counts twenties, and the next set counts three hundred sixties.

beats.on_screen: Given: top to bottom, 2 dots, 3 dots, 1 bar

marks.given: the stack of two dots, three dots and one bar is written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, from top to bottom, two dots, then three dots, then one bar.

marks.find: the words the number shown are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number that the stack shows.

beats.on_screen: read from the bottom: bottom set = 1s, middle set = 20s, top set = 360s

marks.bottom: an arrow starts at the bottom set and the labels 1s, 20s and 360s appear going up

narration: <bookmark mark='bottom'/>Step one, read from the bottom. The bottom set counts ones, the middle set counts twenties, and the top set counts three hundred sixties.

beats.on_screen: bottom: one bar = 5; middle: three dots = 3; top: two dots = 2

marks.mid: the three middle dots are labelled 3
marks.top: the two top dots are labelled 2

narration: <bookmark mark='bar'/>Step two, count each set. The bottom is one bar, which is five.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>The middle is three dots, which is three. <bookmark mark='top'/>The top is two dots, which is two.

marks.expr: 2 x 360 + 3 x 20 + 5 is written, each count joined to its landmark

narration: <bookmark mark='expr'/>Step three, multiply each count by its landmark. We get two times three hundred sixty, plus three times twenty, plus five.

marks.small: 3 x 20 = 60 is written and the parts 720 + 60 + 5 are lined up

narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>Step four, work out the parts. Two times three hundred sixty is seven hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Three times twenty is sixty, and the five ones stay as five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Seven hundred twenty plus sixty plus five makes seven hundred eighty five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the stack
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's reading from the top: 2 x 1 + 3 x 20 + 5 x 360 = 1862; the labels 1, 20, 360 are put on the stack from the top; they are turned to the right way up

marks.doubt: Keeko labels the stack from the top and writes 2 x 1 + 3 x 20 + 5 x 360 = 1862
marks.bottom: the label 1s is moved to the bottom set
marks.fix: the labels are set right and 1862 is crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko reads from the top, so the top set counts ones. That gives one thousand eight hundred sixty two.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>But in the Mayan system the lowest set counts the ones. Each set above counts a bigger landmark.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The five goes with the ones, and the two goes with the three hundred sixties.
